target_statement: Assume a fixed uniform zero-free strip for zeta and determine whether it implies the complete blockwise fixed-delta R68/R71 two-shift estimate.
strip_hypothesis: For some fixed delta in (0,1/2], every nontrivial zero rho=beta+i gamma satisfies delta <= beta <= 1-delta.
candidate_conclusion: On every licensed regular frozen-cutoff block with right endpoint R, X_I <= exp((1-2 delta+o(1))R), where 0<delta<=1/2 is the fixed strip width and X_I is the complete centered energy minus only the grouped atomic diagonal.
control_case: Calibrate the fixed causal-box R95 detector in both directions.
fast_falsifiers: If the zero-side window series is absolutely convergent, the strip should give a pointwise exp((1/2-delta)R) field bound and hence every-block energy control.
If the cutoff-completion error is not subexponential uniformly on the licensed schedule, the strip-to-R68 transfer fails.
If X_I is not bounded above by the nonnegative completed energy, the off-diagonal formulation adds an independent obligation.
If only a growing-order detector is controlled, the reverse R68-to-strip arrow must not be asserted without a varying-test converse.
If the causal-box multiplier vanishes at a possible zero, the scalar control case is not faithful.
quantifier_firewall: delta is fixed independently of R, the block, and zero height
the field retains every cofactor and both mandatory centers
the block weights satisfy 0 <= psi <= 1 and have subexponential support cost
the cutoff schedule is restricted to the range with a proved subexponential Euler-transfer defect
fixed-window and growing-order converse statements are kept separate
nonclaim: This is a conditional calibration. It does not prove the assumed zero-free strip, the R68 estimate unconditionally, or RH.
